notes:
Account summary: Halcyon builds real-time personalization and ad-ranking that require sub-50ms p95 end-to-end for inference path and high throughput (~200–500 qps). Highly cost sensitive due to per-impression economics; strong interest in batching/caching/quantization and explicit benchmarking.

Key technical constraints: network budget to model endpoint ~2–10ms depending on region (edge gateways), must support prefix reuse for short session contexts (60s TTL), KV cache for 1k active sessions, and deterministic fallbacks when capacity constrained. They want per-token cost breakdowns and token-level traceability for billing reconciliation.

What they asked Redwood to prove in POC:
- 72h sustained throughput run showing stable p95 latency <= 50ms for 512-token worst-case chat/rerank flows.
- Cost per 1M tokens using recommended batching + quantization (4-bit/LLM Q8 fallback) configurations.
- Demonstration of prefix/KV cache hit rate improvement and how it reduces effective token counts.
- Fallback policy behavior: route to cheaper model variant when Dedicated capacity saturates and measure quality regression on golden prompt set.

Benchmark specifics requested:
- Harness: custom client that mimics realistic arrival patterns (bursty Poisson + microbursts), 200 unique session keys, 50% requests with 1–4 token prefix reuse. Use both short (<=64 tokens) and long (<=1024 tokens) prompts.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency per-token, end-to-end request latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-request, cache hit ratio, model quality delta on ranked pairs.
- Tools: will accept Redwood's perf harness (preferred) or run internal wrk-based runner and share traces. Instrumentation: token-level timing and token costing tags required.

Security/compliance notes: Halcyon requires SSO + SAML, audit logging for all inference calls, KMS-backed keys with HSM option for private deployments, and EU data residency for European impressions. Legal asked for updated DPA and export controls confirmation.

Commercial posture: leaning toward Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) because of data residency + predictable latency SLAs. Budget range mid-six figures ARR depending on SLA and support SLAs.

Customer quotes: "We can tolerate a small quality delta if cost drops and p95 stays under 50ms — but we need measurable signals to accept tradeoffs."

Next steps (detailed):
1) Redwood to produce an Optimize-run recommendation pack (batching/caching/quantization profiles) by 2025-11-24.
2) 72-hour benchmark scheduled 2025-11-25–2025-11-27, Redwood infra/perf team to coordinate.
3) Post-run results review with data science and infra leads 2025-11-28.
4) Legal to finalize DPA + residency addendum — target 2025-12-05.

Internal notes for AE/SE: prioritize delivering a conservative quantization profile (int4-like) with fallback to q8 for long-context tests; instrument golden prompt evaluation to capture rerank NDCG delta and provide clear cost/quality tradeoff table.
